sources.note: Nothing. Brief background: Bamunka SVO, tense partly marked by grammatical tone, Grassfields Bantu languages 'exhibit highly complex tone systems'; cites 'Sorsamo, H. 2008. The Phonology of Bamunka. SIL Cameroon' for the phonology. No mention of stress. Obtained from Wayback capture (arrow.tudublin.ie viewcontent returns 403 to scripted fetch).

sources.citation: Ngeloh Takwe, Jeannette. 2002. Structural phonology of Bamunka. Post-graduate diploma (maîtrise) dissertation, Université de Yaoundé I, Dept. of African Languages and Linguistics (supervisor Pius Tamanji). vi+93 pp. hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-7F0F-7
sources.note: Nothing. Whole work is a phonology (segments ch.2, syllable structure ch.3, tones and tonal processes ch.4, orthography ch.5). Ch.4 p.56: five phonemic tones (H, L, M, HL, LH), 'Tone in this language is phonemic'. The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur anywhere in the 102-page scanned text layer; pp.40, 56, 81-82 checked on the page images.
